cards.name: Average & Join
cards.summary: Shortcut-only command that does Object > Path > Average (both axes) and Join in one step: two selected open endpoints are moved to their midpoint and fused into one anchor, so two open paths become one continuous path with no gap or overlap.
use_for: closing the gap between two line ends that nearly meet in a traced logo or icon
merging two half-outlines of a symmetric shape (mirrored halves) into one path at the seam
cleaning up open ends before a fill or a Pathfinder operation
avoid: endpoints that sit far apart: averaging drags both to the midpoint and distorts the shape; use plain Join (straight segment) or move one point first
more than two endpoints or whole closed paths selected: it needs exactly two open endpoints, selected with the Direct Selection tool
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("avgAndJoin") with the two endpoints selected (id paired from Defaults.kys by shortcut, some words and order, not confirmed by execution). No DOM call does it in one step; by hand (unverified): the DOM has no join call either, so rebuild one path from both point lists with setEntirePath and put the shared anchor at the average of the two endpoints.

review.changes: script_api pairing note 'by shortcut and order' -> 'by shortcut, some words and order' to match the batch's extra.match (shortcut+some-words+order); script_api no longer implies a DOM join call exists

cards.name: Exit Isolation Mode
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Object/Exit Isolation Mode
cards.summary: Leaves isolation mode: the dimmed artwork outside the isolated group, symbol or path becomes selectable again and the isolation bar at the top of the window disappears. Changes to the artwork are kept; only does anything while a document is in isolation mode.
use_for: returning to the full artboard after editing one group of a crowded illustration
ending a script step that entered isolation mode, so later steps can select across the whole document
avoid: calling it when no isolation is active: there is nothing to exit (Esc or double-clicking empty canvas does the same job by hand)
using it to leave symbol-edit mode after Edit Symbol when you expect it to discard edits: edits are kept
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("exitFocus") (id paired from Defaults.kys by some words and order, not confirmed by execution). No DOM property controls isolation mode.

review.changes: script_api pairing note 'by words and order' -> 'by some words and order' to match the batch's extra.match (some-words+order)

cards.name: Hide Others
cards.summary: Hides every object that is not selected, leaving only the current selection visible on the canvas. Hidden objects stay in the file and come back with Object > Show All.
use_for: looking at one element of a busy layout without moving it to its own layer
clearing visual clutter before checking the outline or alignment of a selected shape
preparing a quick view of one logo variant for a screenshot
avoid: relying on it to remove art from an export: hidden objects stay in the file and can reappear with Show All; delete or move them to a non-printing layer instead
editing one group in context with the rest dimmed: Isolate Selected Object keeps the others visible but untouchable
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("hide2") (id paired from Defaults.kys by shortcut, words and order, not confirmed by execution). DOM route (unverified): set pageItem.hidden = true on every top-level page item that is not selected.

review.changes: script_api pairing note 'by shortcut and order' -> 'by shortcut, words and order' to match the batch's extra.match (shortcut+words+order)

cards.name: Isolate Selected Object
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Object/Isolate Selected Object
cards.summary: Puts the selected group, compound path or symbol into isolation mode: everything else is dimmed and locked, a grey bar appears at the top of the window, and only the isolated object can be selected and edited. The harvest pairs this id with the name by dialog order only, so the id itself is uncertain.
use_for: editing one icon inside a dense infographic without nudging its neighbours
adding new shapes straight into an existing group (new art drawn in isolation joins that group)
tweaking a single sub-path of a compound shape
avoid: trusting the id blindly in a script: it is inferred from the Keyboard Shortcuts order, not confirmed; check that the document actually entered isolation before the next step
wanting the other art hidden rather than dimmed: use Hide Others
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("enterFocus") with one object selected; harvest error: id inferred from the Keyboard Shortcuts dialog order only, not confirmed by execution. No DOM call enters isolation mode.

cards.name: Lock Others
cards.summary: Locks every object that is not selected, so only the current selection can still be clicked, moved or edited; the locked art stays fully visible. Object > Unlock All releases it.
use_for: protecting a finished background or layout while working on one element on top of it
stopping accidental marquee selections of nearby shapes when nudging small details
avoid: expecting a lasting protection: Unlock All undoes it for everything at once; lock a whole layer for longer jobs
needing the other art out of sight: use Hide Others
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("lock2") (id paired from Defaults.kys by shortcut, words and order, not confirmed by execution). DOM route (unverified): set pageItem.locked = true on every top-level page item that is not selected.

review.changes: script_api pairing note 'by shortcut and order' -> 'by shortcut, words and order' to match the batch's extra.match (shortcut+words+order)

cards.name: Repeat Pathfinder
cards.summary: Applies the most recently used Pathfinder operation (Unite, Minus Front, Intersect, Divide and so on) again to the current selection, without opening the Pathfinder panel.
use_for: punching the same knock-out into a row of badges or icons one after another
repeating Divide or Minus Front across many overlapping shape pairs in an illustration
avoid: a fresh session or a different operation: it repeats whatever ran last, so run the wanted Pathfinder button once first
a script that needs a known operation: call that Pathfinder command directly instead of relying on what ran last
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("repeatPathfinder") with two or more overlapping paths selected (id paired from Defaults.kys by shortcut, table, words and order, not confirmed by execution). No DOM Pathfinder API; scripts usually call the specific Pathfinder menu command instead (unverified).

review.changes: script_api pairing note 'by shortcut, table and order' -> 'by shortcut, table, words and order' to match the batch's extra.match (shortcut+table+words+order)

cards.name: Actions Batch
cards.summary: Opens the Batch dialog of the Actions panel, which plays one recorded action on every file in a source folder (or on each data set of the current document) and saves the results to a destination folder.
cards.how: Pick the action set and action, choose the Source (Folder, with options to include all subdirectories and to override Open commands in the action, or Data Sets of the current file), choose the Destination (None, Save and Close, or Folder, with options to override Save and Export commands in the action), and choose whether errors stop the run or are logged to a file.
use_for: exporting a folder of .ai logos to PNG or PDF with one recorded export action
applying the same recolor or outline-text action to a whole set of client files
avoid: an empty Actions panel: record and test the action on one file first
jobs that need per-file logic or naming rules: an ExtendScript loop over the files is more controllable
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe Actions Batch") only opens the dialog (id paired from Defaults.kys by words and order, not confirmed by execution). Scripted equivalent (unverified): open each file with app.open(file), run app.doScript(actionName, setName), save, close.

review.changes: summary/how: Illustrator's Batch source is Folder or Data Sets, not 'all open documents' (that is Photoshop's Opened Files)

cards.name: Add New Fill
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Panel/Add New Fill
cards.summary: Adds another fill attribute to the selected object in the Appearance panel, stacked on top of its existing fill, so one path can carry several fills (for example a solid color with a pattern or gradient over it) without duplicating the shape.
use_for: a solid brand color with a texture or halftone pattern fill layered on the same shape
a gradient sheen over a flat fill on a badge or button
building a reusable multi-fill look to save as a graphic style
avoid: files bound for apps or cutters that only read one fill per path: use Object > Expand Appearance first, or stack separate copies
nothing selected: the extra fill goes to the default appearance for new art instead
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe New Fill Shortcut") with an object selected (id paired from Defaults.kys by shortcut, words and order, not confirmed by execution). The DOM does not expose multiple fills; scripts usually apply a saved graphic style instead (unverified).

review.changes: script_api pairing note 'by shortcut and order' -> 'by shortcut, words and order' to match the batch's extra.match (shortcut+words+order)

cards.name: Add New Stroke
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Panel/Add New Stroke
cards.summary: Adds another stroke attribute to the selected object in the Appearance panel, on top of its existing stroke, so a single path or text object can show several outlines of different width and color.
use_for: sticker-style double outlines around a headline or logo
a thin inner line inside a thick outer stroke for retro badge or neon-sign looks
layered road or rail map lines from one path
avoid: exports to formats or cutters that read one stroke per path: Expand Appearance first
evenly spaced concentric outlines that must be editable as separate shapes: use Offset Path instead
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe New Stroke Shortcut") with an object selected (id paired from Defaults.kys by shortcut, words and order, not confirmed by execution). The DOM exposes only one stroke per path; extra strokes come from a saved graphic style (unverified).

review.changes: script_api pairing note 'by shortcut and order' -> 'by shortcut, words and order' to match the batch's extra.match (shortcut+words+order)

cards.name: New Graphic Style
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Panel/New Graphic Style
cards.summary: Saves the selected object's whole appearance (all fills, strokes, effects, opacity) as a new style in the Graphic Styles panel, so the same look can be applied to other objects with one click. The harvest does not show whether the shortcut opens the naming dialog first.
cards.how: Select an object with the finished look and run the command; if the Graphic Style Options dialog appears, type a style name and click OK. In the panel itself, plain-clicking the New Graphic Style button saves the style without a dialog and Alt-clicking it opens the dialog to name it.
use_for: a brand button or badge look reused across many shapes
keeping a multi-stroke text effect consistent across a poster series
building a style library to apply from scripts with applyTo
avoid: expecting it to save geometry or text: it stores appearance only
styles meant for Photoshop or CorelDRAW: graphic styles do not survive export; expand appearance before handing off
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe New Style Shortcut") with an object selected (id paired from Defaults.kys by words and order, not confirmed by execution); it may stop at the naming dialog. The DOM can only apply existing styles: app.activeDocument.graphicStyles.getByName(name).applyTo(item) (unverified); it cannot create one.

review.changes: how: Alt-click on the panel's New Graphic Style button opens the naming dialog (plain click skips it), not 'Alt-drag skips it'; summary 'swatch' -> 'style'

cards.name: New Layer
cards.summary: Creates a new empty layer above the current layer with the default name (Layer 2, Layer 3 ...) and the next layer color, without opening any dialog; it becomes the active layer for new art.
use_for: separating background, artwork, text and die-line onto their own layers in a print file
starting a new layer for a layout variant or a tracing overlay
avoid: needing a name, color or non-printing/template setting up front: use New Layer with Dialog
wanting a sublayer inside the current layer: use the Layers panel's Create New Sublayer button
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AdobeLayerPalette2") (id paired from Defaults.kys by shortcut, words and order, not confirmed by execution). DOM equivalent (unverified): var l = app.activeDocument.layers.add(); l.name = "Text";

review.changes: script_api pairing note 'by shortcut and order' -> 'by shortcut, words and order' to match the batch's extra.match (shortcut+words+order); equivalents.CDR Object/Objects (opens the Objects docker, makes no layer) -> class:IVGPage (Page.CreateLayer creates the layer); dropped the unsupported 'always top-level' claim from summary and avoid

cards.name: New Layer with Dialog
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Panel/New Layer with Dialog
cards.summary: Opens the Layer Options dialog to create a new layer with its settings chosen up front: name, highlight color, template, show, preview, lock, print and dim-images options.
cards.how: Type the layer name, pick a highlight color, and tick Template (dimmed, locked tracing layer), Lock, Show, Print (untick for a non-printing guide or die-line layer), Preview, or Dim Images to a percentage, then OK.
use_for: a named non-printing layer for die-lines, bleed notes or client comments
a template layer holding a sketch or photo to trace over
named layers that downstream export scripts look up by name
avoid: quick throwaway layers: plain New Layer skips the dialog
scripts: the dialog blocks; create the layer through the DOM instead
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AdobeLayerPalette3") only opens the dialog (id paired from Defaults.kys by shortcut, words and order, not confirmed by execution). DOM equivalent (unverified): var l = app.activeDocument.layers.add(); l.name = "Dieline"; l.printable = false; l.locked = true;

review.changes: script_api pairing note 'by shortcut and order' -> 'by shortcut, words and order' to match the batch's extra.match (shortcut+words+order); equivalents.CDR Object/Objects (opens the Objects docker, makes no layer) -> class:IVGPage (Page.CreateLayer creates the layer)

cards.name: New Swatch
cards.summary: Opens the New Swatch dialog, prefilled with the current fill or stroke color, to save that color as a named swatch in the Swatches panel.
cards.how: Name the swatch, choose Color Type (Process or Spot), tick Global so editing the swatch later updates every object that uses it, set the color mode and values, optionally add it to a CC Library, then OK.
use_for: saving brand colors as named global swatches before building a layout
defining a spot color (Pantone, white ink, varnish, die-line) for print production
avoid: batch-adding many colors: Add Selected Colors or a swatch library is faster
scripts: the dialog blocks; create the swatch through the DOM
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe New Swatch Shortcut Menu") only opens the dialog (id paired from Defaults.kys by words and order, not confirmed by execution). DOM equivalent (unverified): var s = app.activeDocument.swatches.add(); s.name = "Brand Red"; s.color = cmykColor; for a spot use app.activeDocument.spots.add().

cards.name: New Symbol
cards.summary: Turns the selected artwork into a symbol in the Symbols panel via the Symbol Options dialog; the original art on the canvas becomes an instance, and every instance updates when the symbol master is edited.
cards.how: Select the art, press F8, name the symbol, choose Export Type (Movie Clip or Graphic), choose Dynamic (instances can be locally recolored) or Static, set the registration point, optionally enable 9-slice scaling, then OK.
use_for: a logo or icon repeated many times in a layout that must update everywhere at once
map pins, seats or pattern units that are placed dozens of times
keeping file size down when the same complex artwork repeats
avoid: artwork that each copy must alter heavily: break the link or use plain copies
art going to CorelDRAW or Photoshop as symbols: instances usually arrive as plain groups; expand first if exact output matters
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe New Symbol Shortcut") opens the Symbol Options dialog (id paired from Defaults.kys by shortcut, words and order, not confirmed by execution). DOM equivalent (unverified): var sym = app.activeDocument.symbols.add(sourceArt); then app.activeDocument.symbolItems.add(sym) to place instances.

review.changes: script_api pairing note 'by shortcut and order' -> 'by shortcut, words and order' to match the batch's extra.match (shortcut+words+order)

cards.name: Show Color Panel (Secondary)
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Panel/Show Color Panel (Secondary)
cards.summary: Shows the Color panel; from the name it appears to be a second, separately bindable entry for the panel that Window > Color (F6) also opens. What it does differently from the primary command is not established by the harvest.
use_for: binding a second key to bring up the Color panel for mixing or picking a fill or stroke color
avoid: scripts: it only changes the workspace; set colors directly on the objects instead
assuming different behavior from Window > Color: unconfirmed
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe Color Palette Secondary") (id paired from Defaults.kys by words and order, not confirmed by execution). UI-only; no DOM equivalent needed.

cards.name: Update Link
cards.summary: Reloads the selected linked (placed) file from disk, so a photo, PSD or PDF that was edited outside Illustrator shows its current version; the placement, scale and crop in the layout are kept.
use_for: refreshing a product photo after it was retouched in Photoshop
picking up a revised logo or chart placed as a linked file before final export
avoid: embedded images: there is no link to update; use Relink in the Links panel to replace them
a missing or moved source file: relink to the new location instead
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Adobe Update Link Shortcut") with a linked item selected (id paired from Defaults.kys by words and order, not confirmed by execution). DOM equivalent (unverified): placedItem.relink(placedItem.file);
